findings.title: Compile error: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() called with no arguments
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with zero arguments, but the only method with that name is defined in the superclass UsernamePasswordForm as `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which requires a UserModel parameter. There is no zero-arg overload anywhere in the changed files. This will not compile, breaking the build for the whole module.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() requires a non-null user, inverting the intended condition and breaking the primary (non-reauth) passkeys flow
findings.body:
`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. It is used in `authenticate()` (line 115) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137) to decide whether to call `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)`, which sets up the conditional-UI/passkeys attributes (challenge, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI, allowed authenticators) on the rendered form.

Previously this fill was done specifically when `context.getUser() == null` (the normal, non-reauthentication login scenario, e.g. fresh login page, invalid-username error, or empty-password error before the user object is set on the context). With the new `user != null` requirement, `fillContextForm` is skipped exactly in that common case, since `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.getUser()`/`badPasswordHandler()` never call `context.setUser()` before the failing scenario is rendered back. This means the conditional-UI passkeys form data will not be set up for ordinary (non-reauth) logins or after a username/empty-password validation error, which directly contradicts the PR's own updated test `PasskeysOrganizationAuthenticationTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey()` (expects the webauthn form present after submitting only a username, i.e. before `context.setUser()` is invoked) as well as the pre-existing `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` tests that expect the webauthn form to render on a fresh login page where no user is yet set.

findings.title: Unused import after replacing assertThrows(NoSuchElementException...) assertions
findings.body: The import `org.openqa.selenium.NoSuchElementException` is no longer used in this file: both previous usages (`Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, ...)` in `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey`) were replaced with `MatcherAssert.assertThat(..., Matchers.notNullValue())`. The dangling unused import may trigger checkstyle/unused-import build failures depending on the project's lint configuration.
